title: Real-sum size bound
statement: Let $n$ and $s$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$. We say that $f$ has real-sum size at most $s$ if there is a natural number $t\le s$ such that $f$ is a real sum of $t$ linear threshold functions.
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definition of “real sum of linear threshold functions,” so its exact meaning cannot be made self-contained from the provided definitions.
